title: Identify with confidence using MMO’s species ID cards
authors: Fisheries Management Team, Marine Management Organisation

content.text: Misidentification affects many species. To address this issue, some fisheries management plans (FMPs) have proposed the creation of species identification (ID) cards.
These cards will help fishermen identify and report species more accurately, which is important for monitoring catches and understanding the fisheries.
Help us build a better picture together
At the Marine Management Organisation (MMO), we’re working with the fishing industry to improve our understanding of important quota and non‑quota species.

Through this work, we’ve seen how valuable accurate species information is. Non‑quota species are sometimes recorded using general codes or are mistaken for similar species—something that’s understandable given how alike some of them look.
To support you, MMO has developed a set of simple, practical species ID cards.
Our cards for cuttlefish and octopus have already been in use over the past year, and we’re now expanding the range to include sharks, gurnards and squid.
They’re designed to be quick to use, whether you’re at sea, on the quay or in the marketplace.
Getting species identification right helps build a clearer, more accurate picture of what’s being caught. This supports:
Your knowledge and experience are key to making this information as accurate as possible.
Everyone handling these species can play a part—fishermen, buyers and sellers alike.
Find the cards on our FMP Updates page.
You can save them digitally as PDF files or take a screenshot to keep in your phone’s photos.
You can also print them, but if you’d like free printed copies, contact your local MMO office and they’ll be happy to provide them.
Working together, we can improve the data we rely on and support a strong, sustainable future for the fishing industry.
